title: Presence
description: Who held a territory, and when. A presence attaches an outline to an actor over an interval; the outline itself lives under data/geo/presences/ and is never merged into the record, because imported geometry carries its own licence. Presences are drawn on the map under the events and are reached by clicking one; they are never on the timeline.

actor.description: The actor that held the territory. Must resolve to an active actor (rule 17).

presenceType.description: What kind of thing was there. A crisp outline is only honest for a state; a culture or a sphere of influence is drawn diffusely.

dependencyOf.description: The sovereign, when this territory was not its own. null for an independent presence.

dependencyKind.description: How the territory was held, as the source classifies it. null exactly when dependencyOf is null.

when.description: The interval the outline is valid for. end: null means it reaches the present.

geometry.description: Where the outline is. Geometry is sharded by period, and a presence whose interval spans several shards is written into each of them, so this names every file that carries it and the one key it is filed under.

files.description: Paths relative to data/, sorted. Non-empty, and every file exists and holds the key: rule 17.

capital.description: The seat of government, where the source names one.

confidence.description: Imported state borders in a well-covered period are consensus. The field exists so a hand-made presence can say disputed and be drawn as such.
